gen-silkscreen-gf-telex: Silkscreen is a lo-fi, retro display face with letters strung out like spaghetti, each one standing apart. Telex, with its curvy, unclamped shapes and low stroke contrast, keeps paragraphs loose and easy going down the page.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tenor-sans: Every stroke of Silkscreen, down to its g, keeps one unchanging line weight. Tenor Sans is contemporary, its stroke variation light but visible, and a slightly larger size keeps its c tips from creeping together.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tirra: Tirra reads modern and round, its forms curving like open parentheses. Silkscreen's heading letters lack any pressure swells, but Tirra over a full paragraph stays low in contrast and quiet.
gen-silkscreen-gf-titillium-web: Titillium Web, its stroke ends set far apart, stays approachable and low in contrast beneath Silkscreen's unbroken single-weight lines. The heading shouts retro while the body stays quietly contemporary.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tomorrow: Silkscreen draws its bowls at stem thickness, giving lo-fi display letters a retro, spaghetti-line look. Yet Tomorrow's low-contrast bowls open like a cupped palm of clay, and that difference is what makes the pairing.
gen-silkscreen-gf-trispace: Tubelike, lo-fi and retro, Silkscreen draws constant-weight lines that sit apart like spaghetti. And if the heading goes small its charm fades, while Trispace set large would sprawl, its sparse curves opening outward.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Silkscreen spells things out in lo-fi, retro display letters, each one spaced apart like spaghetti. Tsukimi Rounded adds round, open-parenthesis forms and parallel stroke edges, softening the text without competing.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tuffy: Strands of spaghetti turned into letters: that is Silkscreen, lo-fi and retro, with each glyph standing apart. Tuffy is sketched with a pencil that never presses harder, its s widely parted, giving Silkscreen a quiet partner.
gen-silkscreen-gf-varela: Approachable Varela holds the text, its t sharing one width between crossbar and stem, while Silkscreen supplies the lo-fi, retro heading. Spaghetti lines up top, a wide-mouthed c below.
gen-silkscreen-gf-varta: Lo-fi, retro, and unmistakably display: that is Silkscreen. Silkscreen excels at diagonals matching its uprights, while Varta, low in contrast, does best with big open eyes on every e and a.
